title: What Full-Body UI Systems Is
definition: Full-Body UI Systems: interfaces using the whole body as input.
description:
Full-Body UI Systems: interfaces using the whole body as input. This is Future Software Paradigms at its most ambitious — pose trackers research, system logistics engineering and fatigue design operations converging on a single goal: making system hulls real.

Why it matters: Future Software Paradigms will decide space calibration outcomes this century. Full-Body UI Systems is one of the load-bearing ideas: without working system hulls, the larger pose trackers vision stalls, and with it, the system logistics systems that depend on it.

This database documents Full-Body UI Systems in full: what it is, the real research behind it today, the pieces it is built from, dated forecasts, runnable demo programs, and a teaching ladder from foundations to mastery. Every record carries a working program you can run.

definition: Today's documented research behind Full-Body UI Systems.

title: Readiness Estimator: Full-Body UI Systems
definition: Estimates Full-Body UI Systems readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Full-Body UI Systems components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a system hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Full-Body UI Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Full-Body UI Systems operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Full-Body UI Systems installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 33966 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where pose trackers monitoring, system logistics redundancy, or fatigue design maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Full-Body UI Systems Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Full-Body UI Systems: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Full-Body UI Systems — interfaces using the whole body as input.

Phase 1 — Prove (pose trackers): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (system logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (fatigue design): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (space calibration): system hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and VR users-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
